title: docs(spec): state the #7828 destructive signal set on the `ai.requiresConfirmation` docblock
body:
Fixes #13865

## The drift

The JSDoc on `ActionAiSchema.requiresConfirmation` still listed `confirmText` among the signals that make an action look destructive. Maintainer ruling #7828 (Option A) dropped that leg: `actionLooksDestructive` (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:885-888`) reads `ai.requiresConfirmation` first, in both directions, then `mode === 'delete' || variant === 'danger'`. `confirmText` is not read.

Re-verified on `origin/main` a5b95ee before writing: the function body is exactly those three reads, only four files in `packages/` mention it, and the two sibling carriers (the MCP bridge's tool-annotation block, and the header of `packages/runtime/src/action-execution-destructive.test.ts`) already state the corrected rule. Single-site drift, premise intact.

It is a safety-shaped claim, not a stale comment: an author reading it believed a `confirmText` action would be routed through the HITL confirmation path.

## The rewrite

```
-   * `true` for actions that look destructive (`confirmText` set, `mode:'delete'`,
-   * or `variant:'danger'`). Set explicitly to `false` to assert a destructive-
-   * looking action is safe to run without human approval, or `true` to force a
-   * human-in-the-loop gate on an otherwise-safe action.
+   * `true` for actions that look destructive: `mode:'delete'` or
+   * `variant:'danger'` (#7828 Option A). `confirmText` is dialog copy, not a
+   * destructive signal. Set explicitly to `false` to assert such an action is
+   * safe without human approval, or `true` to gate an otherwise-safe one.
```

Byte budget, measured on the whole JSDoc block: 385 bytes before, 383 after — shrinking, as triage required.

Untouched, as ruled: the `.describe()` string ("Override HITL confirmation for AI invocations."), so `content/docs/references/ui/action.mdx` does not move (`check:docs` and `check:generated` both green below); and `docs/adr/0011-actions-as-ai-tools.md`, which records the decision of its day.

Also checked and deliberately left alone: the misplaced-key guidance for a top-level `requiresConfirmation` (`action.zod.ts:869`). It reads "the AI human-in-the-loop override lives under `ai` ... `confirmText` is the separate UI confirm prompt" — that is correct today. It calls `confirmText` a separate UI prompt, which is the post-#7828 reading, and never presents it as a destructive signal. No edit was needed.

## The pin

`packages/spec/src/ui/action-requires-confirmation-docblock.pin.test.ts` — 6 cases.

It does not pin wording. It extracts two regions and compares them: the JSDoc block attached to `requiresConfirmation: z.boolean()`, and the body of `actionLooksDestructive`. Wording alone rots the way it rotted here, because nothing tied the sentence to the function it describes.

The `confirmText` predicate is sentence-level: a sentence may name `confirmText` only while carrying an explicit negation. That admits the useful correction ("`confirmText` is dialog copy, not a destructive signal") and refuses the shape the drift actually took, a positive enumeration. It is self-tested against the retired sentence verbatim, so it cannot pass by the prose merely falling silent.

Both anchors carry anti-vacuity guards, and the classifier half fails in both directions.

## Reverse verification

Both legs: mutate, prove the mutation reached disk by occurrence count and by blob hash differing from the HEAD blob, run, restore with `git checkout HEAD --` on the absolute path, and prove the restore by the disk hash equalling the HEAD blob plus an empty `git diff HEAD`. Never by an exit code, and never committed. Re-run on the final head 1145b48ca; the script carries a restore trap on EXIT INT TERM with absolute paths.

No dist preflight applies: the pin reads both files as source text with `readFileSync`, so nothing resolves through a package `exports` map and there is no built artifact between the mutation and the assertion.

LEG 1 — restore the retired sentence into the docblock:

```
  grep counts — retired phrase: 1 · corrected phrase: 0
  mutated[leg1]: HEAD=c36532b34 disk=d4bdb9939 (differ ⇒ landed)
  pin exit (mutated): 1
     × presents no positive `confirmText` claim 8ms
AssertionError: a `confirmText` sentence with no negation re-seeds the leg #7828 Option A retired: expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []
      Tests  1 failed | 5 passed (6)
  restored[leg1]: disk hash == HEAD blob c36532b34 · git diff HEAD empty
```

The mutated blob d4bdb9939 is byte-for-byte the pre-fix file — the same blob id this PR's diff header names as the "before" side.

LEG 2 — re-enter the `confirmText` leg in the runtime classifier:

```
  grep count — confirmText in runtime source: 4
  mutated[leg2]: HEAD=5747fcc82 disk=1746fb5a2 (differ ⇒ landed)
  pin exit (mutated): 1
AssertionError: `actionLooksDestructive` reads `confirmText` again — reopen #7828 before the docblock in `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` may name it
      Tests  1 failed | 5 passed (6)
  restored[leg2]: disk hash == HEAD blob 5747fcc82 · git diff HEAD empty
```

CONTROL, restored tree: `Tests 6 passed (6)`, exit 0.

## Gates

Family derived on the final head with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at 1145b48ca (49 commands, change set of 2 paths, three-dot against merge base a5b95ee6e), plus the two the card mandated. All measurements below are on 1145b48ca.

Green (exit 0), the load-bearing ones: whole `@objectstack/spec` suite — `Test Files 453 passed | 1 skipped (454)`, `Tests 12214 passed | 1 skipped (12215)`; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` (its `check:test-typecheck` leg compiles the test layer, so this new file is really typechecked — 54 files, no new pinned signature); `check:generated` (15 artifacts, all green on the built tree, `check:docs` and `check:authorable-surface` among them); `check:api-surface`; `check:docs`; `pnpm check:nul-bytes`; `check:cross-package-test-inputs`; and the other 38 derived commands.

NOT MEASURED, never read as green: `check-test-completeness` (grades a saved `turbo run test` log; the family names it with no argument, which is its own documented not-measured branch) and four gates that need a workspace-wide build this container has no reason to do — `check-dev-prereqs`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt`, and `@objectstack/lint`'s `check:doc-formula-expressions` (unbuilt `@objectstack/formula`). Five spec gates that first reported the unbuilt-dist prerequisite were re-run after `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` and are green above, `check:api-surface` among them — that one is why the build was worth doing, since it is the gate that would see a JSDoc leaking into the emitted `.d.ts`. It does not.

## One deviation from the suggested file surface, and why it is not one

`check:cross-package-test-inputs` went red on the first draft of the pin: it collects quoted path literals without parsing, so the sibling carrier's path, written in the header prose, read as an undeclared cross-package input. The fix chosen was to name that carrier by package rather than by path.

The alternative was to declare `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts` in `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` and `turbo.json` — the precedent that file's own comments record for `serve.ts`. It was rejected on two grounds: the declaration would be false (it asserts this package's test verdict depends on a file the pin never reads, and would re-run spec's 7-minute suite on every unrelated MCP change), and it would push the diff outside the file surface this card declared. The path that IS read, `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`, is already covered by spec's declared `packages/runtime/src/**` glob, so the real input needed no widening. Gate green after the reword.

## Changeset

None. JSDoc plus one test file: nothing is published and no package releases, so this takes `skip-changeset` per the workflow's own prescription. The `.describe()` string, the JSON schemas, the authorable surface and the reference pages are all unchanged, and `check:generated` proves it.
